title: The Saintess's Past
next_chapter_hook: The blood light in Ye Qing's sleeve was like a death knell, and the Holy Sect's hunt was about to descend—they had less than three hours to catch their breath.

text.content:
The blood light snaked like a serpent, creeping along the pristine white cuff of Ye Qing's sleeve, glaringly dazzling enough to make one's heart palpitate. That was therestriction inscribed into her very marrow by the Holy Sect—each time her emotions fluctuated too intensely, it would remind her with excruciating pain: every fraction of your emotions belongs to the sect.

Chen Ji's gaze turned frosty, but he did not act rashly. He knew better than anyone that this soulrestriction from ancient times, if forcefully broken, would only cause therestriction to backlash against its host. He slowly stepped back half a pace, placing his hand behind his back, while his knuckles secretly calculating within his sleeve.

dialogue.content: (Bitter smile) "Don't... don't touch it. If you forcefully destroy it, therestriction will shatter my soul directly." Ye Qing gritted her teeth, fine beads of cold sweat appearing at her temples, yet still forcing out a wan, bitter smile, "It's just pain for a while, I've long been accustomed to it."

text.content:
Accustomed to it.

These three words fell lightly, yet weighed like a thousand pounds. Chen Ji gazed at the cold sweat continuously beading at her temples, at that smile so pale it was nearly translucent, and somewhere deep in his chest a string was plucked hard—he did not speak, simply retrieving a plain silk handkerchief from his sleeve and handing it over. The gesture was very light, as if afraid to disturb something fragile.

dialogue.content: (Taking the handkerchief, voice trembling slightly) "...Chen Ji, I've never told anyone these things. But since you're asking why I've become like this—" She took a deep breath, her gaze drifting toward the blurry horizon, "I want you to know what kind of monster the person you trust truly is."

text.content: Moonlight flowed like water, pouring over Ye Qing's cold, serene features, gilded with a silver glow. Chen Ji did not urge, merely standing quietly at her side, three feet away—not too near, not too far, just enough for her to feel companionship, yet not touching that invisible barrier. This was the discretion he had cultivated over many years, also his final respect for a shattered soul.

dialogue.content: (Slow, measured voice) "My original name isn't Ye Qing. That was the name the Holy Sect gave the Saintess—meaning 'purify the darkness.' Isn't it laughable? To have someone who crawled out of hell, purify the darkness." She let out a轻笑, yet the smile did not reach her eyes, "My real name... is Ye Wei. Ye Wei was my sister."

text.content:
Ye Wei.

Chen Ji silently repeated this name in his heart. He had seen too many chess pieces crushed by fate, too many ants struggling to survive in chaotic times—he thought his heart had long turned to iron, that nothing could move him anymore. Yet when those eyes brimming with teardrops gazed at him, he found his throat actually tightening.

dialogue.content: (Voice gradually lowering) "We were born in a small village in the Southern Frontier, where famine plagued the land year after year. Our parents starved to death when we were five. That day... people from the Holy Sect came to the village to select Saintess candidates. Any girls withspiritual root had to undergo examination. Ye Wei... she had nospiritual root, but she was afraid of pain, afraid of blood, afraid of everything terrible."

text.content:
Ye Qing's voice began to tremble, the calm shell she had maintained for so long finally cracking. Under the moonlight, her eyelashes fluttered slightly, like the final desperate flaps of a dying butterfly.

Chen Ji still did not utter a sound, only quietly reaching into his breast pocket, touching that scroll of the残破的 Tianji Record—he had no intention of using it, but that familiar tactile sensation could temporarily suppress the emotions churning within him.

dialogue.content: (Voice choking) "The examination for candidates was simple—drip blood into the圣泉. If the water changed color, one hadspiritual root. Ye Wei... in order to keep me from being selected, when no one was looking, dripped her own blood into the圣泉. The water did change color, but the color was... blood-red."

text.content:
Chen Ji's gaze subtly hardened.

He knew the dark side of Holy Sect doctrine—they practiced the 'Blood Sacrifice Path.' If a Saintess candidate forcibly stimulatedspiritual root with her own精血, it could indeed fool the test short-term. But the price was permanent damage to one's foundation, making future cultivation infinitely more difficult, and every full moon night one had to endure the agony of血脉逆流.

That was the path an eleven-year-old girl chose for herself, so her sister wouldn't have to step into the demonic pit.

dialogue.content: (Tears streaming down her face yet forcing herself not to cry) "But the Holy Sect wasn't foolish. They soon discovered something wrong with Ye Wei's blood. According to the rules, those who infiltrated the candidates through deception faced only one outcome—death. That night, people from the Holy Sect built a pyre, to burn her publicly—" Her voice abruptly stopped, her throat seeming gripped by something.

text.content:
She did not continue, but Chen Ji had already guessed the ending.

Infiltrating candidates through血祭 led to only one outcome—death. Ye Wei traded eleven years of her lifespan for her sister's safety, yet was executed by the Holy Sect as a traitor who deceived the sect and betrayed its ancestors. And Ye Qing—that sister who watched her sister burn to death—eventually was still taken into the Holy Sect.

Not as a prisoner, but as the 'Saintess.'

dialogue.content: (Bitter smile) "They said this was the opportunity Ye Wei exchanged her life for. She said, 'Sister, live well.' They used my sister's ashes to knead into a 'Saintess.'" She raised her hand, gazing at her slender, pallid fingers, "These hands are stained with Ye Wei's blood. Tell me, how could I possibly be clean?"

text.content:
The moonlight seemed wounded by these words, quietly hiding behind the clouds. The night grew denser, shrouding the two figures within it.

Chen Ji finally spoke, his voice light yet carrying an unquestionable certainty: "Ye Wei traded her life for you to live, not for you to rot away in guilt. What she wanted, from the very beginning, was simply for you to live well."

dialogue.content: (Dumbstruck) "You... what did you say?" Ye Qing lifted her head, gazing at this man through tear-blurred eyes, seemingly unable to trust her own ears. All these years, everyone in the Holy Sect called her the 'sinner,' the 'traitor's sister,' the 'vile creature who climbed to power atop her sister's corpse.' No one had ever told her—she deserved to live.

text.content:
Chen Ji did not repeat his words. He merely stood there quietly, moonlight carving out his lean silhouette, those deep eyes holding no disgust, no pity, only a nearly stubborn earnestness.

This gaze reminded Ye Qing of many years ago, in that small village in the Southern Frontier, how Ye Wei had looked at her—with such purity, warmth, free from any trace of impurity.

dialogue.content: (Voice trembling) "Chen Ji... would you嫌弃 a Demon Path Saintess whose hands are stained with blood?"

text.content:
This question was asked lightly, yet like a dull blade, it hacked away at Ye Qing's own heart, cut after cut. She dared not meet Chen Ji's eyes—she feared seeing the answer, and feared even more that the answer would be the one she least wanted to face.

The blood light of therestriction had already dimmed, but the pain in her heart was even more acute than before. Some wounds, therestriction could suppress; other wounds could only be watered with tears.

choice.prompt: How should Chen Ji respond to Ye Qing's humble question?

choices.text: Respond with sharp sarcasm and face-slapping
choices.description: Use caustic words to wake her: "What kind of person do you take me for? I, Chen Ji, have never cared about one's origins."
choices.visible_cost: Might make her even more guilty

text.content: Chen Jiscoffed一声, that laugh carrying a hint of mockery, yet not directed at Ye Qing: "嫌弃? If I were going to嫌弃, would I have waited until today?" He paused, his voice suddenly turning cold, "Do you think those people from the Holy Sect are better than me? No, I simply know more clearly than them—one person's worth is never determined by their hands."

choices.description: Calmly dismantle her logic: "Your sister's death is the Holy Sect's evil, not your crime. Every day you live is you seeing this world for her."
choices.visible_cost: May come across as too cold
choices.visible_reward: Help her break free from guilt
choices.risk_hint: Too rational may not be understood

text.content: Chen Ji stood with hands clasped behind his back, moonlight casting his profile in jade-like coldness: "Ye Wei's choice was her own will, the Holy Sect's cruelty is the Holy Sect's罪孽. You throughout have been merely a victim." He turned his head, his gaze falling upon Ye Qing's tear-streaked face, "Besides—if you truly deserved to die, you would have died decades ago. But you didn't. Your survival is the greatest mockery to those who wanted you dead."

choices.description: Reveal your own similar experience: "My hands have何尝没有沾血? On this path, who hasn't walked forward over corpses?"
choices.visible_reward: Let her feel equality and resonance

text.content: Chen Ji was silent for a moment, then did something Ye Qing had never seen—he lifted his sleeve, revealing a gruesome scar on the inner side of his arm. Those were faint golden patterns, like some kind of forcefully erased mark. "This is left by the grudges of those I killed with my own hands." His voice was very calm, "I battle against them every single day, yet I've never thought about dying. So what makes you think you're more special than me?"

Ye Qing stared blankly at the gruesome scar on Chen Ji's arm, her pupils slightly contracting. She was the Demon Path Saintess, had seen the darkest punishments and wounds in this world, yet never imagined that this seemingly calm-as-water man before her actually bore a dark past similar to hers.

In that instant, she suddenly felt she was no longer alone.

The air between the two seemed to stagnate. The moon emerged from behind the clouds, stretching their overlapping shadows long and long. A night breeze brushed past, carrying a faint, ethereal floral fragrance—that was the residual demonic path secret medicine scent on Ye Qing's lapel, cool yet not acrid.

The blood light of therestriction finally extinguished completely, but a new crisis was quietly brewing in the dark. The Holy Sect's surveillance never ceased, and every word, every move between them now could become evidence for future reckoning.

Chen Ji withdrew his sleeve, his gaze sweeping across the distant horizon. There, several pale green spots of light flickered intermittently—those were the Holy Sect's distinctive tracking spiritual crows. He had read about them in ancient texts; these spiritual beings refined from grudging souls could sense spiritual power fluctuations within a hundred-li radius.

"We don't have much time left." He said quietly, his voice carrying a trace of imperceptible urgency, "The Holy Sect's hunt won't stop, and therestriction in your sleeve is the best beacon. After tonight, both of us must prepare—the day we completely撕破脸 with the Holy Sect is merely a matter of time."

Ye Qing took a deep breath, using her sleeve to wipe away the remaining tear stains on her face. When she lifted her head again, those eyes had rekindled with the cold gleam belonging to the Demon Path Saintess—but this time, beneath that cold gleam, there was also a warmth never seen before.

"Chen Ji." She called softly.

"Hmm?"

"Thank you." Her voice was soft, yet every word was clear, "Thank you for being willing to listen to all this. Thank you... for not嫌弃 me."

Chen Ji did not answer. He merely slightly tilted his head, the corner of his mouth lifting in an extremely faint arc—not mockery, not self-mockery, but a near-tender acknowledgment.

He thought of the blurry image on the Tianji Record Fragment: beneath a sky full of stars, a white-robed woman and a blue-robed man standing side by side, beneath their feet the collapsed Holy Sect mountain gate. That was the future three hours later—and the future he was about to protect with his Heavenly Fate Value.

The night deepened, and two figures gradually faded into the distance under the moonlight. And the pale green light points in the distance had already grown nearer and nearer.
